newsitem.title: USA: U.S. blue chips slightly down before Fed decision.
newsitem.headline: U.S. blue chips slightly down before Fed decision.

text.p: U.S. blue-chip stocks were receding at midday Wednesday as caution prevailed just before the end of a Federal Reserve policy meeting.
The Dow industrials softened even though bonds firmed and most analysts were expecting the outcome of the meeting to be no change in U.S. interest rates.
The Federal Open Market Committee, the Fed's policy arm, is expected to announce its decision on rates at about 1415 GMT/1815 EDT.
"There's some caution ahead of the Federal Reserve announcement," Hildegard Zagorski, an analyst at Prudential Securities, said. "There's not too much exuberance."

The Dow Jones Industrial Average, which shifted restlessly between positive and negative ground for much of the morning, was down about 24 points at 7699. It slipped while bonds firmed 8/32 to yield 6.72 percent, and the Nasdaq composite gained about nine points to 1447.
"The market has been all over the place," Alice Hook, first vice president and trader at McDonald & Co, said.
"There is some caution ahead of the FOMC, just in case they raise rates....It's fairly volatile," she said.
The Dow's decline partly reflected concerns about specific issues, rather than interest rate jitters, analysts said.

"Shares of AT&T and Disney are off sharply, so much of the Dow's fall is internally related," said Harvey Hirshhorn, chief economist and investment strategist at Stein Roe and Farnham. "Cyclicals are a little weaker as opposed to the S&P."
AT&T Corp was down 1-1/4 at 35-1/8, while Walt Disney Co's stock lost 1-15/16 to 76-5/8.
STET/Telecom Italia said it was entering a strategic global alliance with AT&T. AT&T President John Walter said it was too early to talk about taking an equity stake in the Italian company.
Disney softened after Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said it downgraded the company's stock to hold from accumulate.
Deutsche Morgan analyst Alan Kassan said he was concerned that Disney's ABC television network might fall further behind NBC and CBS in the ratings for the upcoming fall season.
While the Dow eased, advancing issues on the New York Stock Exchange outnumbered decliners by a 16-to-11 ratio.
Bellwether Microsoft Corp gained, as did Intel Corp after weakness Tuesday. Microsoft was up two points at 126-15/16, while Intel rose 2-1/16 to 127.
Nike Corp shed 2-4/16 to 56-9/16. Late Tuesday, the athletic shoe and apparel maker posted fiscal fourth-quarter earnings of $0.52 per share, just shy of the First Call consensus estimate of $0.53.
Shares of McDonald's Corp were down 1-1/16 at 47-9/16. Analysts expect the company to show a decline of up to eight percent in June same-store sales.
